core_obligations: Part (a) (proof line 7102): the inclusion C_1 -> C_2 is fully faithful by construction, and it is continuous and cocontinuous because coverings in C_2 between objects of C_1 are the coverings of the big site, which is the author's statement that (a) is immediate from the definitions.

Set up the computation (proof lines 7103-7122): note that g^{-1} is restriction, so O_1(U) = O_2(U) = O(U) for U in C_1, and recall that g_!O_1 is the sheafification of the presheaf V -> colim_{V -> U} O(U), together with the two standard manipulations of elements of that colimit.

Surjectivity (proof lines 7125-7131): for h in O(V), the induced morphism V -> X x A^1 exhibits x in O(X x A^1) as an element pulling back to h, and X x A^1 is an object of C_1 by hypotheses (1)(b) and (2).

Injectivity (proof lines 7134-7153): rewrite an element s of the colimit as a single term over X x A^n using the coordinate functions of the maps f_i, then observe that if the sum x_1 + ... + x_n restricts to zero on V then the map f_1 x ... x f_n factors through the hyperplane X x A^{n-1} = V(x_1 + ... + x_n), so s is equivalent to zero, which proves that g_!O_1 -> O_2 is injective as well.
proof_roadmap: Part (a) is immediate from the definitions of the two sites.
Describe g_!O_1 as the sheafification of the colimit presheaf and record how its elements behave.
For surjectivity, use the affine line, an object of C_1 by hypothesis, to realise an arbitrary section as a pullback.
For injectivity, combine finitely many colimit terms into one via a product of the coefficient maps, then use that a vanishing sum factors through the corresponding hyperplane, an object of C_1.
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares structure sheaves for two nested full subcategories C_1 subset C_2 of a big site: the inclusion is fully faithful, continuous and cocontinuous, and the canonical map g_!O_1 -> O_2 is an isomorphism (statement lines 7069-7099). Part (a) is immediate, but part (b) is a real computation of a colimit presheaf: surjectivity uses the affine line, which the hypotheses force to lie in C_1, to exhibit any section as a pullback (proof lines 7125-7131), while injectivity requires rewriting a finite sum of colimit generators as a single generator over a product of affine lines and then observing that a vanishing sum factors through a hyperplane, again an object of C_1 by the closure hypotheses (proof lines 7134-7153). The non-formal content is this use of the closure hypotheses, in particular products with affine space. The claim is H2: one serious colimit computation with both inclusions verified.
